title: Liquid AI releases LFM3, open-weight 2B models including an omni model and decision models
summary: Liquid AI's LFM3 family has six open-weight models of about 2B parameters, including LFM3-Omni-2B and d1-Omni-2B, which returns calibrated decisions without generating text.
body_markdown:
[Liquid AI released LFM3](https://www.liquid.ai/blog/lfm3) on October 27. It is a family of six open-weight models, each about 2B parameters. The text model, LFM3-1.7B, fits in about 1 GB at 4-bit and scores 96.66 on IFEval, ahead of Qwen3.5-9B.

The new idea is the decision model. [d1-Omni-2B](https://huggingface.co/LiquidAI/d1-Omni-2B) is built on LFM3-Omni-2B and takes text, images, video and audio. It generates no tokens. It returns typed answers with calibrated probabilities in one forward pass, in about 5.8 ms per decision on an H100. All [weights are on Hugging Face](https://huggingface.co/collections/LiquidAI/lfm3).

title: Speridlabs releases Idol, an open model that turns one image into a 3D Gaussian splat
summary: Idol generates 3D Gaussian splats with up to a million Gaussians from a single image, runs in 7.2 GB of VRAM, and ships under Apache-2.0.
body_markdown: [Speridlabs released Idol](https://speridlabs.com/research/idol) on October 28. It turns a single image into a 3D Gaussian splat with up to 1,048,576 Gaussians and exports a standard .ply file. Peak memory is 7.2 GB, so it runs on consumer GPUs. In the lab's own benchmark it beats TRELLIS and TripoSplat on SSIM, LPIPS, IoU and CLIP scores for unseen views. One request takes 6.8 seconds on an H100. The [weights](https://huggingface.co/speridlabs/idol) and the [SDK](https://github.com/speridlabs/idol-sdk) are open under Apache-2.0.

title: Underdog's Bark 3.0 hits 4.94% word error in a 163 MB speech model
summary: Underdog released Bark 3.0 on October 21: a 163 MB on-device English speech-to-text model that ties NVIDIA's Parakeet at 4.94% average word error rate.
body_markdown:
[Underdog released Bark 3.0](https://underdog.ai/bark) on October 21, a 0.6B English speech-to-text model in a 163 MB download. It is built from NVIDIA's Parakeet TDT, and the weights are CC-BY 4.0 [on Hugging Face](https://huggingface.co/ConwayResearch/Underdog-Bark-3.0).

It averages 4.94% word error on the Open ASR Leaderboard's seven English sets, matching Parakeet at 2.51 GB and beating Whisper large-v3's 6.04% at 9.26 GB. On AMI meeting audio it gets 7.82% against Parakeet's 9.42%. It transcribes a minute of audio in under 0.25 seconds on a MacBook. The [claimed number one spot is parity on average, not a win](https://runtimewire.com/article/underdog-bark-3-speech-model).

title: Tencent releases WeVisOne-VL, 2B and 4B open-weight perception models
summary: Tencent's WeChat Vision team published WeVisOne-VL on October 22: 2B and 4B models doing detection, OCR, segmentation and matting, under Apache 2.0.
body_markdown:
[Tencent's WeChat Vision team released WeVisOne-VL](https://tencent.github.io/WeVisOne-VL/) on October 22 with no launch post. It ships in 2B and 4B sizes, both built on Qwen3-VL, and covers detection, referring localization, counting, OCR, segmentation and matting in one model. The mechanism is a 9.6M-parameter pixel decoder attached through a single `<OBJ>` token, so masks and alpha mattes come out of plain next-token prediction.

The [paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.31329) reports 81.8 F1 on RefCOCOg test against 77.6 for the best baseline, and 55.3 on LVIS against 50.7. [Weights and code](https://github.com/Tencent/WeVisOne-VL) are Apache 2.0.

title: OpenAI publishes 722 math manuscripts
summary: OpenAI released 722 AI-generated math manuscripts on October 6, including matrix multiplication at exponent 9/4 and integer multiplication below n log n.
body_markdown:
[OpenAI published 722 math manuscripts](https://github.com/openai/math) yesterday, grouped into 372 result families. An unreleased internal model produced them, with about three hours of ChatGPT Pro thinking compute per result across roughly 4,000 posed problems. The claims include [matrix multiplication with exponent at most 9/4](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/main/preprints/Matrix-Multiplication-Nine-Fourths-October-2-2026/paper.pdf), [integer multiplication below n log n](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/main/preprints/Integer-multiplication-below-n-log-n-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), [the irrationality exponent of π is 2](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/main/preprints/The-irrationality-exponent-of-pi-is-2-September-24-2026/paper.pdf), [Catalan's constant is irrational](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/main/preprints/Catalans-constant-is-irrational-September-24-2026/paper.pdf), [deterministic polynomial factorization over prime fields](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/main/preprints/Deterministic-Polynomial-Factorization-over-Prime-Fields-October-4-2026/Deterministic-Polynomial-Factorization-over-Prime-Fields.pdf), and [the circulant Hadamard conjecture](https://github.com/openai/math/tree/main/preprints/The-circulant-Hadamard-conjecture-September-23-2026).

Not all results are verified. Many manuscripts carry no Lean formalization, and OpenAI says those could have issues.

title: An AI-generated song with an animation Claude Opus 5.5 wrote as code
summary: The "I'm Upping My P(doom)" music video pairs an AI-generated track with an animation that Claude Opus 5.5 produced as rendering code rather than pixels.
body_markdown:
[Patryk Perduta posted this music video](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=tfWEFBvogug) this week, and it is worth three minutes. The song is AI-generated. [osmarks wrote the lyrics](<https://docs.osmarks.net/hypha/p(doom)_song_objectively_correct_interpretation>) on an opening verse by MusicPerson, and Udio generated the original track in November 2024. The pop version used in these cuts was re-generated with Suno this month.

The animation is code, not generated pixels. Claude Opus 5.5 wrote the scene code, headless Chrome paints the frames, and ffmpeg encodes them against the audio. [One published repo](https://github.com/mexicat/pdoom-video) holds 17 scenes locked to word-level lyric timing. Opus 5.5 shipped on September 22.

title: VAST AI releases Mira-Scene, single-image reconstruction of editable 3D scenes
summary: Mira-Scene reconstructs an editable 3D scene from one image and scores 0.727 3D-IoU on BlendSwap against 0.520 for SAM3D. Code and a checkpoint are public.
body_markdown: [VAST AI released Mira-Scene](https://vast-eden.ai/?p=mira-scene) last week. It turns a single image into an editable 3D scene where every object is a separate mesh you can move, remove or animate. The [paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.23796) drops sparse pose regression for a Canonical Coordinate Map that sends each object pixel to a surface coordinate in the object's canonical space. On the BlendSwap benchmark it scores 0.727 3D-IoU against 0.520 for SAM3D, trained on only 60K open-source object assets. The [code and the CCM checkpoint](https://github.com/VAST-AI-Research/Mira-Scene) are public. That checkpoint is one stage of the pipeline, not an image-to-mesh model on its own.

title: Tencent Hunyuan and SJTU release AuK, a 1.5B open-weight speech editing model
summary: AuK generates and edits speech from natural-language instructions, scores 2.65 average WER on Seed-TTS-Eval, and ships MIT-licensed with open weights.
body_markdown: [Tencent Hunyuan and Shanghai Jiao Tong University released AuK](https://auk-project.github.io/) on September 9. It is a 1.5B open-weight model for speech generation and editing from natural-language instructions. It edits spoken content, emotion, accent, timbre, speaking rate and pitch, and it also handles enhancement and separation. On Seed-TTS-Eval it reaches 2.65 average WER and 0.795 speaker similarity, ahead of Qwen3-TTS at 3.07 and 0.745, per the [technical report](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.08936). The distilled AuK-Flash runs in 4 steps and is 4.5 times faster. [Code and weights](https://github.com/Tencent-Hunyuan/AuK) are MIT licensed.

title: OpenAI claims finite-time blowup for forced Navier-Stokes
summary: OpenAI says an internal model proved blowup for the forced Navier-Stokes equations on September 8, a day after Alpöge and Buckmaster posted the Euler case. Clay still lists the problem as open.
body_markdown:
[OpenAI announced](https://openai.com/index/navier-stokes-solution/) on September 8 that an internal model proved finite-time blowup for the forced Navier-Stokes equations. That settles alternatives (C) and (D) of Fefferman's official problem statement, not the unforced (A) and (B) that most mathematicians care about. The [Clay Institute still lists the problem as open](https://www.implicator.ai/clay-institute-navier-stokes-openai-proof-claim/).

A day earlier [Alpöge and Buckmaster posted](https://terrytao.wordpress.com/2026/09/07/finite-time-blowup-with-smooth-forcing-term-for-the-incompressible-porous-medium-boussinesq-and-incompressible-euler-equations/) blowup with smooth forcing for Euler, extending the Córdoba and Martínez-Zoroa programme. Both proofs are AI-assisted and formalized in Lean. OpenAI ran about 10,000 agents for 88 hours and 130 billion output tokens, worth roughly $15 million at list API prices.

title: Qwen releases Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, a 125B open-weight preview of Qwen4
summary: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next is open-weight, has 125B parameters with 6B active per token, scores 62.5 on SWE-bench Pro, and previews the Qwen4 architecture.
body_markdown:
[Qwen released Qwen3.8-Flash-Next](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next) yesterday with open weights under the qwen-community-1.0 license. The model has 125B parameters plus 51B of n-gram embeddings and activates 6B per token. Qwen calls it an early preview of the Qwen4 architecture.

It scores [62.5 on SWE-bench Pro against 53.4 for Claude Opus 4.6 Max](https://officechai.com/ai/qwen-3-8-flash-next-benchmarks/), while Opus stays ahead on Humanity's Last Exam at 40.0 to 35.9. Qwen says [training cost about one-ninth of Qwen3.7-Plus](https://the-decoder.com/alibaba-releases-qwen3-8-flash-next-targeting-ultimate-cost-efficiency/). Context is 262,144 tokens natively.

title: Z.ai confirms Ox Alpha is GLM-5.3-Flash, a 320B open-weight multimodal model
summary: Z.ai revealed that the anonymous Ox Alpha model is GLM-5.3-Flash: 320B total, 18B active, MIT weights, 1M-token context and 84.3 on Terminal Bench 2.1.
body_markdown:
[Z.ai confirmed today](https://z.ai/blog/glm-5.3-flash) that the stealth Ox Alpha model is GLM-5.3-Flash. Ox Alpha appeared free on OpenRouter on August 20 with a 1M-token context window and no named owner. It is a 320B-A18B mixture of experts and natively multimodal. [The weights are on Hugging Face](https://huggingface.co/zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash) under MIT.

Z.ai reports 84.3 on Terminal Bench 2.1 and 63.4 on DeepSWE, and says the model [runs entirely on Chinese AI chips](https://x.com/Zai_org/status/2092616204787626030). Those are frontier numbers from a Flash-tier open model.

title: Tencent's Hunyuan3D-Buffalo 1.0 does text-to-3D, editing and understanding in one model
summary: Tencent published Hunyuan3D-Buffalo 1.0 on August 3: text-to-3D, part-level editing and 3D understanding in one model, trained on 87M samples. Weights are not out.
body_markdown: Tencent published [Hunyuan3D-Buffalo 1.0](https://tencent-hunyuan.github.io/Hunyuan3D-Buffalo1.0/) on August 3. One model does text-to-3D generation, 3D understanding and instruction-guided editing. Training used an 87M-sample corpus: 50M text-to-3D pairs, 25M understanding samples and 12M editing pairs. On Edit3D-Bench it raises average F1 from 0.2729 to 0.6515 over the strongest baseline, Steer3D, per the [paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.02711). Human raters prefer its text-to-3D output to TRELLIS, Universe3D and Omni123 in 56.6% of cases. The [code and weights](https://github.com/Tencent-Hunyuan/Hunyuan3D-Buffalo1.0) are not out yet.

title: nyra labs releases CrisperWhisper 2.0, a 2B verbatim speech recognition model
summary: CrisperWhisper 2.0 scores 87.8 disfluency F1 across 10 languages, ahead of ElevenLabs Scribe v2 and Microsoft, and the weights download and run offline for free.
body_markdown:
[nyra labs released CrisperWhisper 2.0](https://nyra-labs.com/crisperwhisper) in late July and posted the [paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.18934) on July 21. It is a 2B-parameter verbatim ASR model that keeps fillers, repetitions and false starts instead of cleaning them up. On their 10-language disfluency benchmark it scores 87.8 F1, ahead of ElevenLabs Scribe v2 at 79.2 and Microsoft MAI-Transcribe-1.5 at 77.5. Mean word-boundary error is 29.6 ms on TIMIT.

The [weights are on Hugging Face](https://huggingface.co/nyralabs/CrisperWhisper2.0_large), free to download and run offline. The stronger Pro variant scores 93.5 F1 but is not part of the free download.

title: Eyeline Labs and Netflix release ID-V2V for identity-preserving video restyling
summary: ID-V2V restyles a video's background and lighting from a single edited keyframe while holding faces, expressions and lip sync fixed. Weights and ComfyUI support are out.
body_markdown:
[Eyeline Labs and Netflix released ID-V2V](https://eyeline-labs.github.io/ID-V2V/) in July. It takes a source video and one restyled keyframe, then propagates the new background, lighting and style across the clip while keeping faces, expressions, gaze and lip sync fixed. The [paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.22830) reports 0.701 AdaFace identity similarity against 0.402 to 0.529 for the baselines.

It builds on VACE and Wan 2.1, and the [weights are on Hugging Face](https://huggingface.co/Eyeline-Labs/ID-V2V). Kijai added [ComfyUI support](https://comfyui-wiki.com/en/news/2026-07-29-id-v2v-comfyui-support) on July 29.

title: OpenAI's unreleased Astra model produces ten results on open math problems
summary: OpenAI published ten proofs on long-open math and TCS problems today, produced by its unreleased Astra model, each shipped with a Lean 4 formalization.
body_markdown: [OpenAI published ten results](https://openai.com/index/ten-advances-in-mathematics/) on open problems in mathematics and theoretical computer science today. An unreleased internal model called Astra produced them, and each problem had seen no progress on the main result for at least a decade. The list includes the first explicit non-sofic group, a disproof of Connes's rigidity conjecture, and an improved asymptotic upper bound for high-dimensional sphere packing. Every result ships with a [Lean 4 formalization](https://github.com/openai/ten-proofs) and a walkthrough of the model's reasoning. [OpenAI puts the total token cost](https://the-decoder.com/openai-announces-its-next-major-model-astra-by-dropping-ten-previously-unsolved-math-solutions/) at about $2,000 at Sol API rates. No outside mathematician has worked through the arguments yet.

title: HKUST's HOMIE puts specific people and objects into generated video
summary: HOMIE personalizes video with reference humans, products and logos, builds on the open Wan2.1-14B and Wan2.2-14B models, and ships code and weights.
body_markdown: HKUST researchers published [HOMIE](https://yiyangcai.github.io/homie-page.github.io/) last week, a method for putting specific people and objects into generated video while keeping their identity. It handles products, logos and multi-view references, and renders text through OCR maps at up to 1280x720. It builds on the open Wan2.1-14B and Wan2.2-14B video models and uses Qwen3-VL-2B-Thinking to read the references, per the [paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.18217). Code and weights are on [GitHub](https://github.com/YIYANGCAI/HOMIE).

title: Microsoft releases Mage-Flow, a 4B image generation and editing model
summary: Mage-Flow generates and edits images at native resolution, handles depth and segmentation, scores 0.90 on GenEval, and ships open under MIT.
body_markdown: [Microsoft released Mage-Flow](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.19064) last week. It is a 4-billion-parameter native-resolution model for image generation and editing, and it also handles depth, segmentation, Canny, and sketch conditioning. It [scores 0.90 on GenEval](https://aiweekly.co/alerts/microsoft-ships-mage-flow-4b-claims-geneval-lead-on-flux2), first among open models, ahead of FLUX.2 and Qwen-Image at 0.87. The Turbo variant makes a 1024x1024 image in 0.59 seconds on one A100. The weights are on [Hugging Face](https://huggingface.co/microsoft/Mage-Flow) under an MIT license, with code on GitHub.

title: Anthropic releases Claude Opus 5, beating Fable 5 on most benchmarks at half the price
summary: Claude Opus 5 shipped July 24, 2026. It outscores Fable 5 on most benchmarks at half the input price, though Fable stays ahead on SWE-bench Pro.
body_markdown: [Anthropic released Claude Opus 5](https://www.anthropic.com/news/claude-opus-5) today. It beats Fable 5 on most benchmarks at half the input price, $5 per million tokens against Fable's $10. On Frontier-Bench v0.1 it scores 43.3% to Fable 5's 33.7%. On ARC-AGI-3 it hits 30.2%, three times the next-best model. Fable stays ahead on a few, including [SWE-bench Pro](https://benchlm.ai/benchmarks/swePro), where Opus 5 trails at 79.2% versus 80%. [Decrypt](https://decrypt.co/374305/claude-opus-5-outscores-fable-5-most-benchmarks-half-price) reports it becomes the default model for most Claude subscribers.

title: Nvidia releases ARDY, an open real-time text-to-motion model
summary: ARDY generates 3D human and humanoid motion from text in real time; code is Apache 2.0 and weights are open, which could help generate synthetic motion data.
body_markdown: Nvidia [released ARDY](https://research.nvidia.com/labs/sil/projects/ardy) on July 10. It is an autoregressive diffusion model that generates 3D human and humanoid motion from text prompts and kinematic constraints in real time, streaming frames as it computes them. The [code is Apache 2.0](https://github.com/nv-tlabs/ardy) and the [weights are open](https://huggingface.co/collections/nvidia/ardy) under the NVIDIA Open Model License, which permits commercial use. The work is a SIGGRAPH 2026 paper. Open code plus open weights make it a candidate for generating synthetic motion data.

title: Claude Fable produces a counterexample to the Jacobian conjecture
summary: On July 19, 2026, Levent Alpöge announced a Claude Fable counterexample to the Jacobian conjecture: a map with constant Jacobian determinant -2 and no inverse.
body_markdown: On July 19, 2026, Harvard mathematician [Levent Alpöge announced](https://x.com/i/status/2079028340955197566) that the [Jacobian conjecture is false](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jacobian_conjecture), crediting Claude Fable with the counterexample. It is a polynomial map ℂ³ → ℂ³ with constant Jacobian determinant -2 that sends three distinct points to (-1/4, 0, 0), so it has no inverse. The conjecture had been open since Keller posed it in 1939. The announcement was a one-line tweet posted during the World Cup final. The map is elementary to check by hand.

title: Demis Hassabis proposes a FINRA-style body to regulate frontier AI
summary: In a July 14 manifesto Google DeepMind CEO Demis Hassabis called for a US-led, industry-funded AI standards body that could vet frontier models before release and even pause the industry.
body_markdown: [Demis Hassabis published a manifesto](https://x.com/demishassabis/article/2076957440109625718) on July 14 calling for an independent AI standards body modeled on FINRA. Hassabis runs Google DeepMind and shared the 2024 Nobel Prize in Chemistry for AlphaFold. Frontier labs would share models with the body up to 30 days before release, tested for cyber, bio, and deception risks. [He told Axios](https://www.axios.com/2026/07/14/demis-hassabis-ai-regulation-google-deepmind) he wants it US-led, industry-funded, and running before year-end. The body could later require models to pass before US deployment and even [coordinate a slowdown across the labs](https://techcrunch.com/2026/07/14/deepmind-ceo-calls-for-an-independent-standards-body-to-regulate-frontier-ai/). Hassabis says AGI is probably only a few years away. Nadella and Altman back the idea.

title: Moonshot AI releases Kimi K3, a 2.8-trillion-parameter open-weight model
summary: Kimi K3 is the largest open-weight model so far, scores near Fable 5 on the Intelligence Index, and tops the blind-voted Frontend Code arena.
body_markdown: [Moonshot AI released Kimi K3](https://www.kimi.com/blog/kimi-k3) on July 16. It has 2.8 trillion parameters and is the largest open-weight model so far. On the blind-voted [Frontend Code arena](https://lmarena.ai/leaderboard) it is first at 1,679, ahead of Claude Fable 5 and GPT-5.6 Sol. On the broader [Artificial Analysis](https://artificialanalysis.ai/) Intelligence Index it scores 57, just behind Fable 5 at 60 and Sol at 59. It is on kimi.com, subscription and API at $3 per million input tokens and $15 per million output. The weights open on July 27.
